messages:
elaine_finance: Noticing a weird delta in today's AR file: ~90 invoices have an extra platform_fee line reducing net revenue. Numbers don't match Stripe payouts.

ryan_recon: Can you paste an example invoice id? I'll diff ledger vs invoice lines.

elaine_finance: INV-2026-1453 shows two platform_fee lines of $3.00 each. Stripe charge for that invoice only had one application_fee_amount.

ryan_recon: Strange. Could be webhook retrying + double write. Do we log stripe_event_id when creating fee rows?

devon_sre: Quick check: our webhook consumer returns 2xx as soon as it queues a background job. If the job fails and the webhook retries, we might write again. We used to de-dupe at job execution by checking charge_id, but charge_id exists before fee line insertion on some code paths.

elaine_finance: So race condition: ack early -> background job error -> stripe re-delivers -> fee inserted twice.

cfo_jess: This impacts recognition for the quarter if not fixed. Need mitigation ASAP.

ryan_recon: Proposed mitigation steps: 1) Pause netsuite_sync to stop pushing dup lines upstream. 2) Add an idempotency guard keyed by stripe_event_id in fee insertion path. 3) Backfill-dedupe recent duplicates and prepare JE reversals for NetSuite.

elaine_finance: Please pause netsuite_sync and nightly_billing until we've verified fixes. @sync-bot please.

sync-bot: Command accepted: pause job netsuite_sync; pause job nightly_billing at 2026-03-24T09:12:03Z.

devon_sre: I'll change the webhook handler to verify stripe signature, return 200 only after job enqueues AND marks event_id processed (persisted). That prevents retries from causing double writes even if background job fails. Also add a unique constraint on (stripe_event_id, fee_type).

ryan_recon: For cleanup, here's a SQL to identify likely duplicates across last 5 days (uses window function):

```sql
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT id, charge_id, application_fee_cents, created_at,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY charge_id, application_fee_cents ORDER BY created_at) as rn
  FROM invoice_fee_lines
  WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '5 days'
)
SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1;
```

elaine_finance: Good. Once we have a list, I can prepare NetSuite reversal CSV. Note: we need original JE refs for audit.

devon_sre: I'll add a small safe-delete script that tags duplicates with 'candidate_for_reversal' instead of deleting, so finance can review before NetSuite JE. Example patch: insert into fee_dedupe_candidates (fee_id, reason, discovered_by) select id, 'dup_event', 'webhook_hotfix' from ranked where rn > 1;

cfo_jess: Make sure to log all changes and get sign-off before any NetSuite postings. Accounting needs the CSV + short memo.

ryan_recon: I'll run the discovery query and attach CSV to this thread in ~30m. After devon pushes the idempotency patch, we'll run a dry run of dedupe to confirm counts match.

devon_sre: Hotfix timeline: patched handler + migration for unique index in 45m, tests then deploy. Also adding a webhook integration test that replays the same signed payload multiple times and asserts only one fee row gets created.

elaine_finance: Once hotfix is live and we've vetted the candidate list, we'll create JE reversals for the subset already posted to NetSuite. For any invoices not yet synced, keep them in the candidate table so sync ignores them.

ryan_recon: FYI I spotted one edge case: if application_fee_amount is null (legacy charges) our grouping logic must treat nulls as zero to avoid skipping dedupe. Will include coalesce(application_fee_cents,0).

cfo_jess: Thanks. Please include an executive summary with root cause, impact (# invoices, $ amount), mitigation, and timeline after remediation.

elaine_finance: Will do. Tagging FIN-812 (webhook idempotency) and FIN-813 (dedupe & NetSuite reversals). React when you see this so I know you've read. :eyes:

devon_sre: :thumbsup:

ryan_recon: :thumbsup:
